add.text: The Ring of Fire does not extend across the southern Pacific from New Zealand to the Antarctic Peninsula or to the southern tip of South America, because the plate boundaries there (the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge, East Pacific Rise and Chile Ridge) are divergent instead of convergent.
By 85 to 70 million years ago the Izanagi plate had moved north-eastwards and was subducting under east Asia and North America, while the Farallon plate was subducting under South America.
It has been proposed that Vista Alegre and the nearby Vargeão structure formed as a double impact, given their proximity, age and stratigraphic similarities.
The Vista Alegre crater is a meteorite crater in Coronel Vivida, Paraná State, Brazil.
Dryolestids are known from the Jurassic through Early Cretaceous of the Northern Hemisphere and from the Late Cretaceous through the Miocene of South America.
Meridiolestida is an extinct clade of mammals known from the Cretaceous and Cenozoic of South America and possibly Antarctica.
The Mississippi embayment became a primary focus of sediment deposition during the Miocene (about 23 to 5.3 million years ago), which built the foundation of the modern delta region.
The Mississippi embayment is a physiographic feature in the south-central United States, part of the Mississippi Alluvial Plain.

One source dates the appearance of Crocodylia to 83.5 million years ago in the Campanian, and calls them the closest living relatives of birds, the two groups being the only known survivors of the Archosauria.
The wider crocodilian total group, Pseudosuchia, appeared about 250 million years ago in the Early Triassic and diversified during the Mesozoic.
The Sannine Formation localities, together with Sahel Alma, are known as the Fish Beds of Lebanon.
The Sannine Formation and its fossil fishes have been known since Roman Phoenicia.
Mosasaurs breathed air, were powerful swimmers and were well adapted to the warm, shallow inland seas of the Late Cretaceous.
Mosasaurs became extinct in the K-Pg event at the end of the Cretaceous, about 66 million years ago.
Before erosion, the Madagascar flood basalts covered approximately 1,000,000 km2.
The flood basalts consist of lava flows, dykes, sills and intrusions, with plugs, scoria and spatter cones among other volcanic features.
The timing of the origin of ticks is uncertain, though the oldest known tick fossils are around 100 million years old and come from the Cretaceous.
A 2019 analysis suggested that the last common ancestor of all living ticks lived around 195 million years ago in the Southern Hemisphere, in what was then Gondwana.
Blood-feeding evolved independently at least six times in arthropods during the late Cretaceous; in ticks it is thought to have evolved 120 million years ago.
Carnosaurs are distinguished by large eye sockets, a long narrow skull, and leg and pelvis modifications such as a thigh bone (femur) longer than the shin (tibia).
Most former carnosaurs, such as the megalosaurids, spinosaurids and ceratosaurs, have been reclassified as more primitive theropods.
An anoxic event is a period in which large expanses of the oceans were depleted of dissolved oxygen, creating toxic waters that were both anoxic and sulfidic (euxinic).
An oceanic anoxic event can be viewed as the Earth's response to excess carbon dioxide injected into the atmosphere and hydrosphere.
Unlike more primitive iguanodonts, hadrosaurid teeth were stacked into complex dental batteries that acted as effective grinding surfaces.
Hadrosaurids were facultative bipeds: the young of some species walked mostly on two legs and the adults mostly on four.
Hadrosaurids descended from Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous iguanodontian dinosaurs and had a similar body layout.
The Praia Grande crater lies in the Santos Basin, about 200 kilometres southeast of the São Paulo State coastline.
It is a possible impact crater identified on 3D seismic data by Petrobras in 2004.
The igneous rocks formed in the second phase have a geochemical makeup similar to intra-plate composition.
The flood basalts in the Canadian Arctic Islands are similar to the Columbia River flood basalts of the Pacific Northwest of the United States.
During the late Paleocene, around 60 million years ago, parts of the Ninety East Ridge were exposed for 2–3 million years as volcanic islands, probably 1,000 km from the nearest land.
The ridge shows no systematic isotopic variation, which is inconsistent with an ageing mantle plume origin for all of it; this suggests at least two separate hotspots contributed.
The Ninety East Ridge area, besides being related to the hotspot, lies on the diffuse boundary between the Indian plate and the Australian plate.
The fifteen volcanoes of the eight principal Hawaiian islands are the youngest in a chain of more than 129 volcanoes stretching 5,800 kilometers across the North Pacific Ocean.

In 1963 John Tuzo Wilson hypothesized that the chain was made by an essentially stationary volcanic hotspot as the Pacific plate drifted northwest, leaving a trail of increasingly eroded islands and seamounts.
Palms (Arecaceae) were the first modern family of monocots to appear in the fossil record, around 108 million years ago in the Early Cretaceous, earlier than the date given here.
In 2001 uranium-lead dating by the Geological Survey of Finland estimated the crater's age at around 73.3 million years, with a margin of error of five million years.
Velociraptor was a small dromaeosaurid that lived in Asia from about 75 million to 71 million years ago.
Velociraptor was about 1.5–2.07 m long with a body mass of around 14.1–19.7 kg, smaller than Deinonychus and Achillobator.
Velociraptor is distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long, low skull with an upturned snout.
The Manson impact was one of the largest known impact events in North America.
The impact structure has no surface evidence because it is covered by comparatively recent glacial till, and the site is now a flat landscape.
In 1991 and 1992 the U.S. Geological Survey and others researched the structure in part to test a possible connection with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction.
Bennettitales were among the most common seed plants of the Mesozoic, with shrub and cycad-like forms.
The exact position of Bennettitales among seed plants remains uncertain.
A massive fall in sea level would have greatly reduced the continental shelf margin, which could have caused a mass extinction for marine species only.
Some argue sea level fall was the most likely cause because the boundary layers show no distortion or tilting related to mountains.
Sea level fall as a cause is contradicted by evidence that sections showing no sign of marine regression still show a major drop in diversity.
Mosasaurus competed with other large predatory mosasaurs such as Prognathodon and Tylosaurus that fed on similar prey, but coexisted with them through niche partitioning.
Another source gives Mosasaurus a range of about 82 to 66 million years ago, across the Campanian and Maastrichtian.
Mosasaurus had robust jaws with dozens of large cutting teeth, and a high metabolic rate suggesting it was endothermic.
Multituberculates were the most diverse order of Mesozoic mammals, with more than 200 species ranging from mouse-sized to beaver-sized.
By the early Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) the Cimolodonta had replaced all other multituberculate lineages.
One source says the Labrador Sea formed as the North American and Greenland plates separated, starting about 60 million years ago (Paleocene) and stopping about 40 million years ago.
Spreading in Baffin Bay and the Labrador Sea slowed, became oblique, and ceased between 45 and 36 million years ago.
The type specimen, found in 1971 in the Javelina Formation of Texas, consists of several wing fragments and was described as Quetzalcoatlus northropi in 1975.
Quetzalcoatlus northropi is a candidate for the largest flying animal ever found, though its size is hard to estimate because the only known specimen is fragmentary.
Azhdarchids like Quetzalcoatlus were highly terrestrial by pterosaur standards, though even the largest could fly.
Belemnites were an important food source for many Mesozoic marine creatures, both adults and planktonic juveniles.
Pterosaurs are an extinct clade of warm-blooded flying reptiles, not dinosaurs, which are defined as descendants of the last common ancestor of Saurischia and Ornithischia.
The Shiva crater is a proposed impact crater on the Indian continental shelf, offshore west of Mumbai.
Chatterjee proposed that Shiva, Chicxulub and other possible craters came from multiple impacts that caused the end-Cretaceous extinction.
The accretion of Chaitenia to Patagonia occurred in the Devonian (c. 400–360 million years ago), inferred from an event of pressure, deformation and heating dated to that period.
After Chaitenia merged into Patagonia, accretionary complexes developed to its west, so Chaitenia acted as a backstop.
Radiodonts were among the earliest large predators, and also included sediment sifters and filter feeders.
Until the 2010s radiodonts were considered uniformly large apex predators, but new species discovered that decade greatly widened their known diversity.
Through convergent evolution, lungfishes evolved internal nostrils similar to the tetrapods' choana.
The first tetrapodomorphs, lungfishes' closest kin, had the same general anatomy but appear not to have left the water until the Late Devonian.
By the middle of the Devonian, several groups of vascular plants had evolved leaves and true roots.
During the Devonian free-sporing land plants spread across dry land, forming extensive coal forests that covered the continents.
